text: Amantadine is a weak uncompetitive NMDA-receptor antagonist; the Gocovri label states that its therapeutic mechanism is unknown and distinguishes anticholinergic-like adverse effects from demonstrated direct anticholinergic activity. (low confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: The February 2026 Gocovri label warns against abrupt withdrawal because of worsening parkinsonism and neuropsychiatric symptoms; for treatment longer than 4 weeks it advises, if possible, halving the dose for the final week. (low confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: The 2003 Cochrane amantadine review found insufficient evidence for efficacy and safety for general idiopathic Parkinson symptoms from older trials; its searches extended through 2001, so that conclusion does not include the 2017 EASE LID dyskinesia trial. (medium confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: The February 2026 Gocovri label starts treatment at 137 mg at bedtime and increases after one week to 274 mg at bedtime; it explicitly states that Gocovri is not substitutable with other immediate-release or extended-release amantadine products. (low confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: EASE LID excluded patients with MMSE scores below 24, estimated glomerular filtration rates below 50 mL/min/1.73 m2, and prior amantadine intolerance or lack of response; these exclusions limit direct generalization to such patients. (low confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: Gocovri renal dosing is formulation-specific: the February 2026 label recommends 68.5 mg initially and a maximum of 137 mg daily for moderate impairment, 68.5 mg daily for severe impairment, and contraindicates use in end-stage renal disease below 15 mL/min/1.73 m2. (low confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: NICE recommendations tagged 2017 advise against vitamin E as neuroprotective treatment, restrict co-enzyme Q10 neuroprotective use to clinical trials, and advise against creatine supplements in Parkinson disease; these adjunct supplements should not be presented as established neuroprotective therapy. (low confidence) (verified as of 2017-07-19)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: In the 2017 EASE LID trial, the week 12 placebo-adjusted improvement in Unified Dyskinesia Rating Scale score was 7.9 points. This is evidence for the studied extended-release product and population, rather than proof that every amantadine formulation is equivalent. (medium confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: The February 2026 Gocovri label indicates this extended-release amantadine product for dyskinesia during levodopa-based treatment and as adjunctive treatment for off episodes; these are product-specific indications. (low confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: Hallucinations, peripheral edema and dizziness were prominent adverse events in EASE LID; Gocovri prescribing information also lists these adverse reactions. (medium confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: The February 2026 Gocovri label warns that concomitant drugs with anticholinergic properties may potentiate anticholinergic-like adverse effects; it advises reducing the anticholinergic drug or Gocovri dose if atropine-like effects appear. (low confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: Benztropine and trihexyphenidyl are anticholinergic options used particularly in younger patients; cognitive impairment, confusion, hallucinations, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and urinary retention restrict their usefulness, especially with advancing age. (medium confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs

text: The Parkinson Foundation describes anticholinergics as predominantly useful for tremor with little effect on other symptoms; the Cochrane review found motor benefit over placebo but conflicting results and insufficient support for a preferential effect on tremor. The latter limits claims of established symptom selectivity. (medium confidence)
keywords: Amantadine, anticholinergics and other adjunct drugs
